changes.after: A class tells you what kind of object a value is.

before: An integer, string, true, false and nil are all objects. A value’s class describes its kind of object.
value.class calls the method named class on that value. A method is a named operation an object can respond to; this call reports Integer or String here.
An ordinary local variable can later refer to an object of another class. Reassignment is different from modifying the original object.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
value = 7
puts value.class
```
Expected output or behavior: Integer. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Inspect the classes of several values without guessing from how their text looks. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A class tells you what kind of object a value is.

The output is `Integer`. Ruby calls this whole-number class Integer.

before.question: Replace 7 with "7". What prints?
choices: Integer because the text contains a digit.
String because the value is quoted text.
Float because all quoted digits become decimals.
before.explanation: The new literal creates a String object, not an Integer object.

after.question: Which class would the quoted seven have?
after.explanation: Ruby calls a text value a String.
